evidence_summary: Effects Database groups Applied Banshee Wah and the Crown, Guild VW-1, Jax-USA, Kadent, Magnum, and V-Jay wah variants under an Applied Wah Wah OEM family. The family is kept distinct from the FW-3 combined fuzz-wah platform.
Applied Banshee Wah is cataloged inside the Applied Wah Wah OEM family. It is treated as a wah/volume product state separate from the Applied Banshee Fuzz and from the FW-3 combination pedal.
Effects Database explicitly identifies the Guild VW-1 as an Applied-family wah and gives a 1972-1978 Guild catalog window. Guild remains the marketed identity.

Jax-USA Wah is listed as a member of the Applied Wah Wah OEM family. The available source is family-index evidence rather than a model-specific factory statement, so it remains below the high-confidence tier.
Kadent Wah Wah is listed within the Applied Wah Wah OEM family. The relationship is retained as a marketed state until model-specific period documentation improves.
Magnum Wah Wah is listed within the Applied Wah Wah OEM family. The evidence supports family membership but does not yet establish a precise production window for this branded wah.
V-Jay Wah Wah is listed within the Applied Wah Wah OEM family, while the V-Jay FW-3 has separate high-confidence Applied production evidence. The two V-Jay products are not merged into one model.
Effects Database places Hohner WW-20 beneath the Applied Wah Wah OEM family. It is not promoted as a fully confirmed Applied production state until model-specific documentation is located.
The Jax-USA FW-3 is explicitly described as manufactured in the United States by Applied Audio and sold under the Jax-USA name as part of the Applied OEM line.
The Atlantic FW-3 is explicitly described as manufactured by Applied Audio in the United States and as sharing the Applied FW-3 platform; Atlantic is retained as the marketed label.
The Magnum FW-3 is explicitly described as manufactured in the United States by Applied Audio and as part of the Applied FW-3 OEM series.

The Nomad Fuzz Wah is explicitly described as manufactured by Applied Audio and is grouped with the Applied FW-3 family. This record is kept separate from the unresolved Nomad Super Fuzz/Fuzzrite question.

Tone Machines documents Applied-made Nomad effects being distributed by LIMMCO Inc. The record is intentionally classified as a commercial distribution relationship, not as evidence that LIMMCO physically built the pedals.
